clue.text: Struggled to capture queen if checked

indicators.note: to capture means to take something and hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: struggled in the sense of competed, contended
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the standard abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: A chess player battled to take the opponent's queen, wondering whether the king was in check.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture makes 'checked' look like part of the game, a king in check; it is the definition, meaning confirmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something verified has been confirmed as true after examination, just as a checked fact has.

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
plus is read as the word and

indicators.note: the minus sign means the second set of letters is subtracted from the first

parts.note: this time six is written out as the word six
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A mock sum whose result is food.
explanation.walkthrough: The '—' (minus) takes IX (nine in Roman numerals) from the word SIX, leaving S. The two sixes are read differently, one Roman, one spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: Viands is an old word for items of food, provisions.

clue.text: Chores are set for a maiden, perhaps

indicators.note: set means arranged or put in order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Household jobs are assigned to a young unmarried woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges CHORES ARE. A MAIDEN is a horse that has never won a race, not a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing a maiden is a horse yet to win, so it is one example of a thoroughbred runner.

clue.text: Feminine look freed a part of America

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
rid means freed, as in got rid of

explanation.surface: A woman's appearance liberated part of the US.
explanation.walkthrough: LO is an archaic call to look, as in 'lo and behold'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sunshine State is one of the United States, so part of America.

clue.text: Stops for execution and rests

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Stops for execution and rests' (5), gives no parse for EASES: 'stops for execution' suggests STAYS (stays of execution), which crossing E from 1-across rules out; no blog or database found to settle it.

clue.text: This bird married a doctor — one with bearing

parts.note: M is the usual abbreviation for married, as on forms
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
the Roman numeral I stands for one
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A bird marries a physician who has a certain bearing or deportment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' suggests posture or manner but is a compass point, E for east.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-white thieving corvid of folklore is a familiar bird.

clue.text: Almost hoping to get a drug

indicators.note: almost means not quite the whole word, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: aspiring means hoping or aiming for something

explanation.surface: Wishing for a medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the last letter, G, from ASPIRING.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetylsalicylic acid is a common painkilling medicine.

clue.text: Sit on year end problem

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose

indicators.note: end points to the final letter of the word year

explanation.surface: Someone sits on the problem of how to close the financial year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'year end' looks like an accounting phrase but gives R, the final letter of 'year'; 'on' places it after POSE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is a puzzling question, a tricky problem.

clue.text: Writer's one way to support attempt

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting pieces sit underneath, after the word for attempt

parts.note: an essay is an attempt, as in essaying a task
I is one in Roman numerals
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A writer's single method of backing an effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer's' is the definition plus 's (is). In a down clue 'to support' puts I and ST below ESSAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who composes short prose pieces is one kind of writer.

clue.text: Signs for season in Australia

indicators.note: in means the word for season goes inside the abbreviation

parts.note: to season food is to spice it, and spice is seasoning

explanation.surface: Looking for signs of the changing season in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'season' looks like a time of year but is the cook's verb or noun, SPICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Auspices were omens read from birds in ancient Rome, hence signs or portents.

clue.text: Pelicans could be showing confusion!

definitions.meaning: a pelican is a type of pedestrian crossing in Britain, whose function is to let people cross the road
describes people who misunderstand each other, each pursuing a different aim

explanation.surface: Large waterbirds seem to be acting in a muddled way.
explanation.walkthrough: A PELICAN crossing is a British signal-controlled pedestrian crossing; read literally, such crossings exist for the purpose of crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes two parties talking past each other, a state of mutual misunderstanding; literally, it is what road crossings are built for.

clue.text: Had terrible trouble returning — started sending flowers

indicators.note: terrible signals that the word had is mangled into a new order
returning signals that the word for trouble is read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

indicators.note: started points to just the beginning of the word sending

explanation.surface: Someone had a dreadful time coming back and has begun to send flowers as an apology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' makes DAH from HAD; 'returning' turns AIL into LIA; 'started' takes S from 'sending'.
explanation.definitionFit: These are showy garden blooms of the daisy family, named after the botanist Dahl.

clue.text: Describe harbour light

parts.note: a port is a harbour for ships
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: An instruction to describe the light seen over a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: To depict someone in words or pictures is to describe them.

clue.text: Supply weapons to a good number, and bill for drink!

parts.note: to arm someone is to supply them with weapons
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Arming a large group of people and then sending them the bill for alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' is AC (account), not a beak or a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagnac is a brandy from Gascony, a strong alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Refinements found in French resort with connections

parts.note: Nice is the resort city on the French Riviera
ties are bonds or connections

explanation.surface: Elegant manners discovered at a Riviera resort with good contacts.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine points of etiquette or detail are subtle refinements.

clue.text: Cuts that affect prisons?

definitions.meaning: small cuts or notches made in a surface
nick is British slang for a prison or police station

explanation.surface: Spending cuts that hit the prison service?
explanation.walkthrough: 'that affect' joins the two senses; NICK is everyday British slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Small notches are tiny cuts, and in British slang a nick is a jail.

clue.text: Racists on exchange get breakfast in France

indicators.note: on exchange means the letters are swapped around into a new order

explanation.surface: Bigots trading insults over a French breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange' rearranges RACISTS ON; 'on' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescent-shaped flaky pastry is the classic morning meal item in France.

clue.text: Lithe cat becomes very active

indicators.note: becomes signals that these letters turn into something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A supple cat turns very lively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becomes' rearranges LITHE CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fit, energetic and sporty is very active.

clue.text: Evidence of crying out loud after rows

indicators.note: out loud signals that the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: tears are the visible evidence that someone has been crying

explanation.surface: After a series of arguments, someone is heard sobbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' looks like quarrels, which suits the crying, but it means lines, as in tiered seating.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiers are layers or ranks arranged one above another, like stacked lines of seats.

clue.text: One learns of Parisian in thrilling exploit

indicators.note: in means the French word sits inside the word for exploit

parts.note: a stunt is a daring, thrilling feat
de is the Parisian, that is French, word for of

explanation.surface: A student of the French capital caught up in a daring escapade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Parisian' means 'of' as a Parisian says it, DE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is studying is one who learns.

clue.text: Players' club made of this?

parts.note: the cast are the players in a production
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: Asks what an actors' club or golfer's club might be built from.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a golf club could be made of this hard metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard brittle alloy poured into moulds, a plausible material for a metal golf club.

clue.text: Definitely not yet representing one without faith

indicators.note: not means the letters of yet are excluded from the pool
representing signals the remaining letters are rearranged to stand for something new

explanation.surface: Definitely not yet a believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes Y, E, T from DEFINITELY, leaving DFINIEL, which 'representing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbeliever, someone who rejects a given religion, is one lacking faith.

clue.text: Climbers lose head, seeing snakes

indicators.note: lose head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: ladders are things you climb, climbers in a cryptic sense

explanation.surface: Mountaineers panic when they spot vipers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbers' suggests mountaineers but is LADDERS; 'lose head' drops its L. Snakes and ladders is a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is Britain's only venomous snake, a viper.

clue.text: A case of something to wear in court?

definitions.meaning: a legal action brought before a court
a joking reading: an outfit for a law court

explanation.surface: A legal case, or what a barrister might wear before the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal action is a case; split in two, it reads as a court outfit.

clue.text: The earth's span, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: span is an old past tense of spin, meaning whirled

explanation.surface: The size of the planet, as reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'span' looks like a measure of extent but is the archaic past of spin; 's is the link 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Our planet is commonly called this, as in travelling round it.

clue.text: Denied having joined again

definitions.meaning: fused a second time, welded back together

explanation.surface: Someone was turned away after having rejoined a club.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-FUSED, the word means melted together once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To be denied is to be turned down; split with a prefix, the word means bonded a second time.

clue.text: Inflexible us soldier protected by free

indicators.note: protected by means the soldier sits inside the word for free

parts.note: to rid is to free
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An unbending American serviceman shielded by a liberated people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'us' here is US, the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stiff and unbending is inflexible.

clue.text: Man's speciality event?

parts.note: the Isle of Man's emblem is a triskelion of three running legs, so its own sports-day event would be the one run in tied pairs

explanation.surface: Asks which sporting event a man excels at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, whose flag shows three armoured legs joined at the thigh.
explanation.definitionFit: A school sports-day contest in which partners run with adjacent legs tied, fitting the Manx emblem.

clue.text: Students of French in musical

indicators.note: in means the French word goes inside the musical's title

parts.note: Cats is the long-running Lloyd Webber musical
de is French for of

explanation.surface: Students of French performing in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Students of French' looks like one phrase but splits: 'Students' is the definition and 'of French' is DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainees at a military or police academy are students of a kind.

clue.text: USA dealt out praises

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: America dealt out compliments to its allies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges USA DEALT.
explanation.definitionFit: To flatter lavishly is to praise excessively.
